title: Powered confirmation: does expert-forecaster elicitation fix the certified advertising-as-harm sign inversion? (#342)
context: Certified reader-roleplay run: visit direction_accuracy 0.0 (sign-inverted), heterogeneity rank_rho -0.29 at chance. Exploratory 6-case forecaster probe: Sonnet visit dir_acc 0.0->1.0, Spearman -0.29->+0.65. This confirms at power.
design: Finer stratification gender(3) x recency-tier(3) x email(2) from the real Hillstrom RCT CSV; real per-cell visit uplift = ground truth (cells >=300/arm). Expert-forecaster elicitation (Sonnet + Groq), VISIT outcome. Label-permutation p-value (5000) on Spearman.

hypotheses.H1 (sign-fix): Sonnet expert-forecaster visit direction_accuracy >= 0.85 (vs certified reader-roleplay 0.0)
hypotheses.H2 (heterogeneity): Sonnet visit Spearman rho > 0 with permutation p < 0.05

decision_rule: If H1 holds at n>=12 -> the advertising-as-harm sign inversion is FIXED by elicitation framing, certified at power on real RCT ground truth (the report's #1 accuracy problem). If H2 also holds -> visit heterogeneity ranking recovered. Honest null reported if either fails.
ground_truth: computed from local Hillstrom CSV (MineThatData 2008), not the simulator
